post.summary:
Repairs saga membership for movies that belong to no collection: their
sequels are already in the library, but membership is only written while
a title is enriched, so anything enriched before that path existed never
joined its saga. Returns immediately; progress shows up as the
"collection_relink" background task.

RemuxAudioLibrary is RETIRED: it always fails with FAILED_PRECONDITION.
See RemuxAudioMedia - this is the bulk form that did the July damage.

MatchOrphansInLibrary targets only items missing provider IDs (TMDB
never matched them at scan time) and queues an async re-enrichment.
Returns immediately with the count of queued items; the enricher
pool drains them in the background under its existing concurrency
and rate-limit caps. Idempotent - re-run to pick up the still-
orphaned remainder once any rate limits clear.

parameters.name: libraryId
parameters.description:
Optional: when set, only items of this library are refreshed.
Empty (default) refreshes every library.

get.summary:
ListMediaRepairs answers "what did the repairs touch" across the whole
library: every journal entry in a time window, newest first, optionally
one batch kind. The 98 files rewritten on 2026-07-13 were only ever found
by a hand-written query on file modification times; this is that
question, asked of the journal, from the health page.

parameters.name: sinceMs
parameters.description: since_ms / until_ms bound the window (unix ms); 0 = open on that side.

parameters.name: job
parameters.description:
job keeps only one batch kind ("reindex", "rollback", "purge",
"fix_container", "scan"); empty = every entry, operator actions included.

get.summary:
ScanSeekIndex returns the cached result of the last completed scan for the
scope - instant, no disk I/O. scanned_at_ms is 0 when no scan has completed
yet; kick one with StartSeekIndexScan and poll GetSeekIndexJob. Files
without an index seek/resume slowly because the player has to scan
linearly; has_backup reports whether a prior reindex left a restorable
.mkvgobak.

parameters.name: libraryId
parameters.description: Optional: when set, only this library is scanned. Empty = every library.

post.summary:
AckSeekIndexMedia records (or withdraws) the operator's acknowledgement of
one file's verdict. Refused (FailedPrecondition) for a repairable file:
what can be repaired is repaired, not waved through.

AckSeekIndexGroup acknowledges every pending file of one verdict
("informational" - the only ackable one) in scope. Returns how many it
marked.

DeleteSeekIndexBackup removes one media's reindex backup (.mkvgobak),
reclaiming the duplicated disk space once the repair is confirmed fine.
Synchronous (an unlink) - no job involved.

get.summary:
GetSeekIndexJob reports the live progress of the running seek-index job
(scan, reindex or rollback) plus a summary of the last finished one.
Poll it after any Start*/Reindex*/Rollback* call.

post.summary:
CancelSeekIndexJob stops the running seek-index job at its next file
boundary (a repair in flight finishes or rolls back; no file is left
half-written) and returns at once. cancelled=false when nothing was
running. Observe the end via GetSeekIndexJob (last.cancelled).

PurgeSeekIndexBackups kicks a background job that re-scans the scope then
deletes EVERY reindex backup in it. Returns immediately; progress via
GetSeekIndexJob.

StartSeekIndexScan kicks a background scan of the library (all libraries
when library_id is empty) and returns immediately. Scanning walks every
MKV/WebM on disk so it can take minutes on a large/network-mounted library
- a synchronous call would time out behind a reverse proxy. Read-only.
Fails with RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED if a seek-index job is already running.

RemuxAudioMedia is RETIRED: it always fails with FAILED_PRECONDITION.
It used to pull every audio track that started after the picture back
onto it by its own declared delay, with no upper bound - which is exactly
how a deliberate dub alignment looks - and rewrote 98 files that way on
2026-07-13 with no surviving backup. An audio start offset is a fact
about a file, measured and shown by the scan (audio_delay_sec,
audio_tracks_lag_sec), never something Evey rewrites. The RPC stays so a
deployed client gets a translated refusal instead of UNIMPLEMENTED.

ApplyAudioShift moves one audio track by an amount a PERSON judged on a
preview clip. Nothing this server measures can say whether the sound
follows the picture - comparing a file's own tracks says only whether they
agree with each other - so this is the one path where a human's ear is the
evidence, and the journal records it as exactly that.

FixContainerMedia renames one .mkv whose bytes are really MP4/MOV to .mp4
and repoints the catalog, in the background (outcome via GetSeekIndexJob).

ReinterleaveMedia re-muxes one file whose tracks are stored in blocks of
one track at a time (see SeekIndexItem.interleave_backstep_sec), in the
background; the original is kept as a backup. Outcome via GetSeekIndexJob.

get.summary:
GetMediaRepairHistory returns what has been done to one file's bytes,
newest first: which operation, on what evidence, and whether it can still
be undone. Evey keeps no copy of a repaired file - the entry itself is the
way back - so this is the only place that history exists.

post.summary:
ReindexMediaSeekIndex rebuilds one media file's seek index in the
background (a rewrite of a multi-GB file takes minutes) and returns
immediately with accepted=true. Outcome is observable via GetSeekIndexJob.
The rebuild is validated + cross-checked before an atomic swap and the
original is kept as a .mkvgobak; on any failure the original is left
untouched. Fails with RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED if a job is already running.

RollbackMediaSeekIndex restores one media file from its .mkvgobak backup
in the background, undoing a prior reindex. Returns accepted=true
immediately; outcome via GetSeekIndexJob. Fails fast if the media has no
file, or with RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED if a job is already running.

UndoMediaRepair replays the file's most recent reversible repair
backwards, from its journal entry. Refused when the last repair discarded
bytes (nothing can bring those back) or was written by a newer version
whose payload this build cannot read safely.

track.description: track is the Matroska track number to move, as listed by the preview.

shiftSec.description: shift_sec is signed: positive delays the track against the picture.

mode.description:
Repair strategy: "inplace" (surgical patch, file-write only, no backup),
"auto" (try the patch, fall back to the rewrite when the file layout
defeats it - backup kept on the fallback), or "rewrite" (full rebuild +
.mkvgobak rollback backup). Empty = rewrite.

deepVerify.description:
deep_verify makes mkvgo prove every rebuilt cue lands on a real video
keyframe before committing (a full read of the file), on top of the
always-on head-only check. A failure rolls the in-place patch back and
aborts the rewrite before its swap. Recommended with "inplace", which
keeps no backup.

skipBackup.description:
skip_backup drops the .mkvgobak of a rewrite once the swap has succeeded,
so the volume never accumulates one extra copy per repaired file - the
option for repairing a nearly-full disk. The server compensates by
forcing deep_verify on. No effect on "inplace" (never keeps a backup).

resync.description:
resync repairs a file the strict reindex REFUSED for a corrupted region
(junk between clusters, a lying size): the tolerant rewrite skips the
damaged span and resynchronises, recovering everything before and after.
It ALWAYS rewrites and forces a backup - this is the one repair that loses
data (the skipped span, logged). For the per-file "repair anyway" action
on a file that failed a normal repair. Overrides mode/skip_backup.

verdict.description:
"informational" - the only verdict one can acknowledge. A repairable
defect is repaired, not waved through.

cancelled.title: a job was running and has been asked to stop

scope.title: "" = all libraries, else the library id

last.title: unset until a first job finishes

libraryId.description:
Optional: when set, only orphans of this library are queued.
Empty (default) targets orphans in every library.

job.description: job names the batch this belonged to, so a whole run reads as one thing.

evidenceMethod.description:
evidence_method says what justified acting: "track-coherence" is a
measurement, "declared-defect" is the file's own claim taken at face
value - the weak case that caused the 2026-07-13 incident.

shiftSec.description:
shift_sec is what was applied per audio track, signed. Its opposite is the
undo, which is why no copy of the original is kept.

reversible.description: reversible: this entry alone carries enough to put the file back.

mediaId.description:
media_id and path name the file, for the cross-library listing where an
entry is not read under one media's row. path is the file as it was
recorded, which survives a media being deleted and re-added.

v1MediaRepairEntry.description: MediaRepairEntry is one rewrite of one file, as recorded when it happened.

libraryId.description: Optional: when set, only this library's backups are purged. Empty = all.

deepVerify.description:
See ReindexMediaSeekIndexRequest.deep_verify. Costs a full read PER FILE,
so a whole-library sweep with it on is a long job.

skipBackup.description:
See ReindexMediaSeekIndexRequest.skip_backup. For a whole-library sweep
this is the difference between one temporary copy at a time and one
PERSISTENT copy per repaired file on the volume.

backupWindow.description:
backup_window (with backups on) keeps only the N most recent repairs'
.mkvgobak while the sweep runs: as the job advances past the window, the
oldest backup is purged automatically, and the job's end drains the
remainder - the volume never holds more than N extra copies and finishes
with none. 0 keeps every backup. Ignored with skip_backup or "inplace".

includeAudio.description:
include_audio also repairs the audio start-delay of every flagged file in
the same job (needs the ffmpeg remuxer wired; ignored otherwise). A file
that also lacks an index is only reindexed this run - its audio waits for
the next, so its true original backup is never clobbered.
include_audio is IGNORED since the triage rework: Repair all repairs every
repairable defect, the audio start delay included. Kept for wire compat.

resyncDamaged.description:
resync_damaged also rewrites, in resync mode, the files whose index is
fine but which carry mid-file corruption: the ONLY way they become
playable, at the price of the damaged bytes. Explicit consent; such
repairs always keep their backup.

queued.description:
Deprecated: the candidate count is only known once the background scan
phase completes - always -1 now. Poll GetSeekIndexJob for done/total.

accepted.description:
The repair now runs in the background; per-file details (backup path,
warnings, sizes) land in the server log and the job summary.

skipped.description: Deprecated pre-async fields, always zero now that the repair is a job.

limit.description: Upper bound on titles examined in this sweep. 0 means the server default.

libraryId.description: Optional: when set, only this library is repaired. Empty = every library.

queued.description: Deprecated: always -1 - poll GetSeekIndexJob for done/total.

restored.description: Deprecated: the restore now runs in the background - poll GetSeekIndexJob.

scannedAtMs.description:
When the last completed scan for this scope finished (unix ms). 0 = no
scan has completed yet - items/counters are empty, not "all clean".

audioDelayed.description: Count with audio_delay_sec above the defect floor (~0.1s).

inplaceAvailable.description: Whether the surgical in-place repair mode is available in this build.

truncated.description:
Count of truncated (incomplete-download) files - these need re-acquiring,
not repairing. Count of files with resync-repairable mid-file damage.

wrongContainer.description: Count of .mkv files that are really MP4/MOV - rename/remux, not reindex.

trailingJunk.description: Count carrying surplus bytes past the Segment end (harmless, a rewrite drops them).

audioShort.description:
Count whose audio ends before the declared duration (re-acquire the
source; playback fills the missing tail with silence meanwhile).

seekCoarse.description:
Count rebuilt and still too coarse to seek into (see seek_coarse). These
are NOT part of missing_index: no repair can improve them.

volumes.description:
Live per-filesystem numbers for the un-indexed candidates, so the client
can advise for/against backups (their accumulation persists the SUM of
the candidates) and flag files whose rewrite temp copy will not fit.

repairable.description:
The triage the page is built on. repairable is exactly what Repair all
acts on; informational counts only the remarks still awaiting the
operator's eyes (acknowledged ones are in acked).

manual.description:
manual is always 0 since the "your call" verdict was removed. Kept only
so an older client keeps parsing; do not read it.

containerFixAvailable.description:
container_fix_available: the server can rename a mislabelled .mkv to .mp4
and repoint the catalog (part of Repair all when true).

brokenInterleave.description: Count stored as blocks of one track at a time (see interleave_backstep_sec).

reinterleaveAvailable.description:
reinterleave_available: the server can re-mux a file stored in blocks
(part of Repair all when true).

audioPictureOff.description: Count whose sound is measured off the picture (see audio_picture_lag_sec).

unreadable.description: Count the scan could not diagnose at all (see unreadable).

hasIndex.title: false = muxed without Cues → slow seek/resume

hasBackup.title: a .mkvgobak exists → a prior reindex is rollback-able

audioDelaySec.description:
Audio starts this far after the video (seconds, max across audio tracks).
Above ~0.1s = repack mux defect playing as a constant A/V desync on
copied audio (transcoded audio auto-cancels it at playback). 0 = aligned.

truncated.description:
truncated = the file is an incomplete download whose damage runs to EOF:
no tool recovers the missing tail, a resync only yields a playable prefix.
The remedy is re-acquiring the source, NOT a repair. Only diagnosed scans
set this (older scans leave it false). Repair the source, not the file.

damagedBytes.description:
damaged_bytes > 0 = mid-file corruption a resync repair skips past, losing
this many bytes (the file is otherwise repairable in full). 0 = clean.

wrongContainer.description:
wrong_container = a .mkv whose bytes are really MP4/MOV. It has no Matroska
seek index to build; the remedy is rename/remux, not reindex. Kept out of
the missing-index bucket so "Repair all" never wastes a doomed reindex on it.

trailingJunk.description:
trailing_junk = surplus bytes past the declared Segment end; the media is
complete (leftover junk, or a crashed in-place-repair journal). Harmless -
any reindex rewrite drops them - so it is NOT damaged_bytes and needs no
re-download. Surfaced on its own so a whole file is never flagged as corrupt
just for carrying tail junk.

audioShortfallSec.description:
audio_shortfall_sec > 0 = an audio track stops this many seconds BEFORE
the VIDEO does (mux defect: dead audio over the credits). Measured against
the picture's real end, not the container's declared duration - that
duration is only a muxer's claim, and an over-stated one made aligned
files look like audio defects. The file is structurally healthy, so no
index/damage check sees it, but players used to die at the wall (playback
now fills the tail with silence). NOT repairable - the audio's tail is
absent from the file; the remedy is re-acquiring the source. Only gaps
past the ~10s defect floor are reported (ordinary muxes leave a couple of
seconds of slack).

missingTailBytes.description:
missing_tail_bytes quantifies truncated: how many declared bytes are
absent from the end of the file. The magnitude routes the decision - a
9 KB stub is invisible in playback, 41 MB is a missing final scene.

seekCoarse.description:
seek_coarse = the index was rebuilt and is STILL too coarse to seek into:
the encode's own keyframes sit further apart than a seek can tolerate, and
no index can be denser than the keyframes it names. Reported apart from
missing_index precisely so it stays OUT of the repair queue - offering a
repair that cannot change anything is what pinned 134 prod files. The
remedy is a re-encode or a better source, and it is offered as a remark
(informational verdict), never as an instruction.

verdict.description:
verdict is the ONE answer per file, and there are only two non-healthy
ones: "repairable" (Evey repairs it here - Repair all acts on exactly
these) and "informational" (something we measured and mention, possibly
wrong, never a chore). Informational files can be acknowledged.
The former "manual" verdict is GONE: a detector that cannot repair
something has not earned the right to hand the operator an instruction.

ackedAtMs.description:
acked_at_ms > 0: the operator acknowledged this file's verdict (it stays
out of the attention list until the file's bytes change).

seekCoarseDetail.description:
seek_coarse_detail is the diagnoser's own account of the remaining hole
("the video cues leave a 44s hole - ...") - often the final credits alone.

audioTracksLagSec.description:
audio_tracks_lag_sec is how far this file's OWN audio tracks disagree once
their declared offsets are applied, in seconds, and it is what decides
whether audio_delay_sec matters. Two tracks of one film share their music
and effects bed: they line up when the offsets are RIGHT (a dub aligned to
its cut - nothing to do) and disagree when a track sits in the wrong place.
0 with audio_tracks_checked true means PROVEN coherent.

audioTracksChecked.description:
audio_tracks_checked says the comparison actually ran, so a 0 lag reads as
"proven coherent" rather than "never looked". It runs on every file with
two or more audio tracks; false when the file has one audio track, or the
two mixes shared no legible signal.

audioTrackZeroed.description:
audio_track_zeroed is the fingerprint of a track that was retimed onto the
picture: one audio track starts at exactly 0 while a sibling keeps its
small priming offset. A muxer treats sibling tracks alike; only a repair
that pulled ONE track back by its own declared delay leaves this shape
(the 2026-07-13 batch). It names the touched file; the amount removed is
gone from the file and nothing here can restore it. Informational.

resyncRequired.description:
resync_required = a repair ALREADY ran on this file and the strict rewrite
refused it: the source is structurally corrupt somewhere the scan never
looked. The scan is head-mostly on purpose (7 000 files must not each cost
a full salvage walk on a NAS), so this class of damage is only ever
discovered BY a repair - and before this field the answer was thrown away
with the error, leaving the operator a raw Go string and no button.
It means "only a resync can repair this", exactly like damaged_bytes > 0,
with one difference that must not be blurred: the amount a resync would
drop is UNKNOWN here, so it is never folded into the damaged byte total.

interleaveBackstepSec.description:
interleave_backstep_sec > 0 = the tracks sit in separate blocks of minutes
(video alone, then audio alone): the largest step BACKWARDS of the cluster
timestamp between two sampled positions. No sequential player gets past
the first block; only a re-mux by timestamp fixes it. Informational.

audioPictureLagSec.description:
audio_picture_lag_sec is the measured offset of the worst audio track
against the PICTURE, read off the file's own subtitles (positive = the
sound must move later); audio_picture_track is that track's ordinal and
audio_picture_checked says the measure ran and concluded. Informational:
the operator applies the value with the preview.

unreadable.description:
unreadable = the scan could not diagnose this file at all: missing or
unreadable on disk, or a container the parser refused. Every other flag
is unset and has_index is true so it never enters a repair queue;
unreadable_detail is the error in the prober's words. Informational: the
operator re-acquires the file or fixes the mount. Such a file used to be
dropped from the scan with a log line - the sickest files of a library
were the ones the health page never showed.

v1SeekIndexItem.description: SeekIndexItem is the per-file diagnosis surfaced by ScanSeekIndex.

readOnly.description:
The failure came from a read-only mount (:ro media volume) - the user
must remount read-write before repairing.

v1SeekIndexJobFailure.description: SeekIndexJobFailure records one file a job could not process.

scope.title: "" = all libraries, else the library id

skipped.title: files that already had an index (nothing to do)

error.title: job-level error (e.g. the scan itself failed)

readOnly.title: at least one failure came from a read-only mount

cancelled.description:
cancelled: the job stopped at a file boundary on request (the cancel RPC
or the server going down); done < total is not a failure here.

v1SeekIndexJobSummary.description: SeekIndexJobSummary describes the last finished job (since server boot).

largestMissingBytes.title: floor for one rewrite temp copy

v1SeekIndexVolume.description: SeekIndexVolume aggregates the repair candidates of one filesystem.

libraryId.description: Optional: when set, only this library is scanned. Empty = every library.

pace.description:
How much of the media disks the scan may take:
  "gentle" (default, and what anything unknown means) - one file at a
    time, then a stand-aside as long as the file just took to read. The
    disks stay free about half the time, so playback survives the scan.
  "fast" - several files at once, no pause. For a library spread over
    several disks, where one file at a time leaves the other spindles
    idle; expect the disks to be busy for the whole run.

shiftSec.description: shift_sec is what was applied to undo, per track.
